Factoring the constant out of the integral, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{5}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =5{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\cdot \text{arctan}\,x\,{|}_{1}^{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =5(\text{arctan}(\sqrt{3})-\text{arctan}(1)) \\  & =5(\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =5(\frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$
